Objectives: The entire area of the Bowen burn would be closed to livestock grazing for a minimum of two years. This includes: Meadow Divide, Holbrook Burn, North Bowen, and South Bowen pastures.\r\n\r\nThis closure is an administrative action and does not require Emergency Stabilization funding.
Planned_Implementation: The PFO\u2019s range staff would ensure that the affected pastures/allotments are administratively closed to livestock grazing.\r\n\r\nEffectiveness will be monitored by the PFO Range Program. Ensuring vegetation recovery objectives are met prior to the resumption of livestock grazing will ensure an effective closure.
Actual_Implementation: There were a few head of livestock found in the burned area because of fires this year. During the initial stages of the 2007 Cow Canyon fire several fences were cut in an attempt to save cattle located in the fires path. This forced several head of livestock into the closed area, but after the fire was controlled the livestock were promptly removed and only a few isolated head were found after that.

Objectives: To protect the burned areas from unauthorized livestock use in order to help ensure vegetation recovery.
Planned_Implementation: To ensure that the agreement is written and presented to the permittee.
Actual_Implementation: A handful of sites were reviewed by an Interdisciplinary Team to evaluate reintroduction of grazing to those select pastures.  Cover, seedhead production counts, and grass pulls to test rooting strength were used to evaluate the recovery of these sites and to help determine if they could withstand grazing.  The results were written into memos outlining the criteria for reintroduction of grazing, and the terms to be held up while grazing occurs, such as duration, timing, and utilization percentages.  The East 71 Pasture of Grassy Hills AMP Allotment and Turner Cedar Butte Allotment have met the criteria established post Murphy Fire and are scheduled to be reopened in the fall of 2008.  Other sites have been identified for review in late August and early September, and are being analyzed currently.  If the criteria for reopening are met, then the pastures will be open during their normal seasons of use.  In 2009, all of the sites will have the grazing reintroduction monitoring performed in addition to the normal monitoring procedures, unless grazing has been implemented at that site prior to the second year of monitoring.\r\n\r\nThe Natural Recovery sites which were rested to livestock grazing in order to aid in recovery area recovering as expected in the first year following a fire.  Four areas have been identified as needing treatment in the form of herbicide control for cheatgrass and seeding the appropriate seed mix for the site.  These sites will be monitored as seeding treatments following treatment.  Erosion is an issue at some sites, but appears to be minimizing.  Further monitoring is needed to determine if a trend towards natural recovery is being made.
Treatment_Effect_and_Results: Effectiveness monitoring will include visits to the site by range staff and other BLM employees to ensure that there is no livestock within the burned area and that no unauthorized use has taken place.
